content.title: Is Hulu down? Oscars TV confusion as users report problems watching ceremony on Disney Plus accounts
content.text: HULU subscribers were left confused as they tried to tune in for the 98th annual Academy Awards. The Oscars kicked off at 7pm ET on Sunday, but Hulu customers were panicking over whether the popular streaming platform was down during the biggest night in Hollywood. Sign up for The Irish Sun newsletter Thank you! The Oscars, hosted by Conan O’Brien, kicked off Sunday night at 7pm ETCredit: EPA Hulu customers have reported issues with the streaming service during the live eventCredit: SOPA Images/LightRocket via Gett The Oscars streamed live on ABC News and Hulu as millions sought to see which films and actors would take home the prestigious awards. But Hulu subscribers took to social media, wondering if there were issues with the platform. Hulu Support said on X that the Oscars will be streaming live for “all Hulu subscribers on the Hulu app or website.” “The replay will also be available on demand on Disney+ after the ceremony ends.” One user replied to Hulu’s post, furious that the ceremony didn’t properly play for some of those with a Disney+ bundle, saying, “This makes zero sense! “So Hulu subscribers can watch The Oscars live but people who have HULU in their Disney+ plus bundle won’t have a live stream??” The X user said Hulu told her there is a “workaround,” which allowed her to use her Disney+ login in the Hulu app. The social media user suggested activating Hulu in the Disney+ account settings first if others have an issue accessing The Oscars. Most read in Entertainment Who won on Hollywood’s biggest night? One Battle After Another ran away with the night with six Oscars, while Sinners, which was nominated for a record-breaking 16 awards, came away with four. See the full winners list below: Best Picture: One Battle After Another Best Actress: Jessie Buckley, Hamnet Best Actor: Michael B. Jordan, Sinners Supporting Actress: Amy Madigan, Weapons Supporting Actor: Sean Penn, One Battle After Another Directing: One Battle After Another, Paul Thomas Anderson Adapted Screenplay: One Battle After Another, Paul Thomas Anderson Original Screenplay: Sinners, Ryan Coogler Documentary Feature: Mr. Nobody Against Putin Documentary Short: All the Empty Rooms Animated Feature: KPop Demon Hunters Animated Short: The Girl Who Cried Pearls Cinematography: Sinners, Autumn Durald Arkapaw Costume Design: Frankenstein, Kate Hawley Film Editing: One Battle After Another, Andy Jurgensen International Feature: Sentimental Value – Norway Life Action Short: The Singers (TIED) Two People Exchanging Saliva (TIED) Makeup and Hairstyling: Frankenstein, Mike Hill, Jordan Samuel and Cliona Furey Original Score: Sinners, Ludwig Goransson Original Song: Golden, KPop Demon Hunters Production Design: Frankenstein, Tamara Deverell and Shane Vieau Sound: F1, Gareth John, Al Nelson, Gwendolyn Yates Whittle, Gary A. Rizzo and Juan Peralta Visual Effects: Avatar: Fire and Ash, Joe Letteri, Richard Baneham, Eric Saindon and Daniel Barrett Casting: One Battle After Another, Cassandra Kulukundis Others took to social media asking Hulu, “Why is there literally not an option for me to watch the Oscars?” The streaming giant told viewers they would need to be subscribed to one of its Hulu + Live TV plans to watch the livestream. Those who wanted to tune in for shocking moments, like when Timothee Chalamet was roasted by host Conan O’Brien for his comments that “no one cares” about opera or ballet, could watch on ABC if they were still having issues with Hulu. Viewers could also have streamed the award show on the ABC website and App. Other streaming platforms, such as YouTube TV, DIRECTV Stream and FuboTV, carried the live broadcast that wrapped up a little after 10:30pm EST.
